metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (COBOL) with a deployable entry point (PROGRAM-ID. PAYRUN) executed via JCL job scheduling on z/OS mainframe. Single service with persistent data access.
metadata.archetype_justification: Reads from indexed employee master file (persistent state) and writes payroll output (state mutation). No message queue consumers, no multi-service orchestration.

findings.title: Managed Compute — all compute on z/OS mainframe
findings.description: All compute runs on an IBM z/OS mainframe (COBOL batch) with an EC2 m4.large file gateway. No managed container orchestration or serverless.
findings.gap: Zero adoption of managed compute services. Mainframe runtime requires full platform shift.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite payroll logic in modern language and deploy to ECS Fargate or Lambda. Replace EC2 file gateway with AWS Transfer Family.

findings.title: Managed Databases — self-managed DB2 on mainframe
findings.description: Database is IBM DB2 for z/OS v10, self-managed on mainframe. Application reads from indexed VSAM file.
findings.gap: All persistent data on self-managed mainframe storage. No managed database with automated failover or patching.
findings.recommendation: Migrate employee data to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS and SCT.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — hardcoded in JCL
findings.description: Workflow orchestration handled entirely by JCL job steps and CA-7 mainframe scheduler. Two-step sequential workflow with no managed orchestration service.
findings.gap: All workflow logic hardcoded in JCL. No retry logic, no error handling, no visual workflow management.
findings.recommendation: Implement payroll workflow using AWS Step Functions with error handling and retry logic.

findings.title: Async Messaging — no messaging, file-based FTP only
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. Cross-system integration via plaintext FTP file transfer to EC2 gateway.
findings.gap: No managed messaging for cross-system state propagation. File-based FTP is sole integration mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Replace FTP with event-driven patterns: EventBridge/SNS for notifications, S3 for file delivery with event notifications.

findings.title: Network Security — no VPC, plaintext FTP with PII
findings.description: No VPC, subnet, or security group configuration. EC2 gateway receives plaintext FTP with PII (SSN, bank accounts). No network segmentation or encryption in transit.
findings.gap: No network security controls. Plaintext FTP transmits sensitive payroll data with no encryption.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in VPC with private subnets. Replace FTP with AWS Transfer Family (SFTP) or S3 over HTTPS. Implement least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: API Entry Point — no gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or managed entry point. Batch system with direct FTP exposure to EC2 gateway.
findings.gap: No managed entry point providing throttling, authentication, or traffic management.
findings.recommendation: Expose migrated services behind API Gateway with Cognito auth. Use AWS Transfer Family for file transfers.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — all capacity statically provisioned
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Compute statically provisioned on z/OS mainframe and single EC2 m4.large. Batch window overruns indicate capacity constraints.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned with no dynamic scaling to address growing workload.
findings.recommendation: Deploy on ECS Fargate or Lambda for inherent auto-scaling. If EC2, configure ASG with scaling policies.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — no backup configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found. JCL uses GDG for output versioning but no formal backup strategy, no PITR, no cross-region replication.
findings.gap: No automated backups, no retention policy, no restore procedures documented.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated backups on managed databases with minimum 7-day retention and PITR. Enable S3 versioning.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code — zero coverage
findings.description: Zero IaC coverage. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. Infrastructure changes manual, non-reproducible, undocumented in code.
findings.recommendation: Define all AWS infrastructure in Terraform or CDK: VPC, subnets, compute, database, security groups.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD automation. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodePipeline. All deployments manual via mainframe JCL and CA-7.
findings.gap: All deployments manual. No build, test, or deployment automation.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD with AWS CodePipeline + CodeBuild. Include build, test, and deploy stages with automated rollback.

findings.title: Programming Languages — COBOL with no cloud-native tooling
findings.description: Enterprise COBOL 4.2 on z/OS. No AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, no modern framework ecosystem. Requires mainframe runtime.
findings.gap: COBOL fundamentally incompatible with cloud-native development. No AWS SDK, no containerization support.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in modern cloud-native language: Python, Java 17+, or TypeScript with first-class AWS SDK support.

findings.title: Monolith — tightly-coupled single COBOL program
findings.description: Single COBOL program with all business logic in one linear flow. No module boundaries, no interfaces, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, no service interfaces, no independent deployment or scaling capability.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite as separate services: data access, calculation engine, output generation. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: Async vs Sync — all communication synchronous
findings.description: For stateful-crud archetype: all communication synchronous. Sequential file I/O and synchronous FTP. No async messaging or event-driven patterns.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous. State changes cross system boundaries via blocking file transfer.
findings.recommendation: Implement event-driven patterns: publish payroll events to EventBridge/SNS, deliver results via S3 with event notifications.

findings.title: Long-Running Process — 5-7 hour batch with no checkpointing
findings.description: For stateful-crud archetype: batch job runs 5-7 hours with no async processing, no status polling, no checkpointing, no resume capability.
findings.gap: Long-running batch handled as single synchronous operation. No checkpointing or resume-from-failure.
findings.recommendation: Implement chunked processing with checkpointing. Use Step Functions or SQS fan-out for parallel processing.

findings.title: API Versioning — no versioning on any interface
findings.description: No API exists. Only interface is 120-byte fixed-width flat file with no schema definition or versioning.
findings.gap: No versioning on any interface. Flat file format undocumented and unversioned.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning from day one. For file outputs during migration, define schema with version headers.

findings.title: Service Discovery — all endpoints hardcoded
findings.description: Hardcoded IP address (10.0.7.40) for EC2 gateway FTP. Hardcoded dataset names in JCL. No service discovery or DNS-based routing.
findings.gap: All endpoints and resource locations hardcoded in JCL.
findings.recommendation: Use environment variables or SSM Parameter Store for endpoints. Implement Cloud Map for service discovery.

findings.title: Unstructured Data — locked in mainframe file systems
findings.description: All data on mainframe file systems (VSAM) and transferred via FTP to local EC2 storage. No S3, no managed object storage.
findings.gap: Data locked in mainframe VSAM files and local EC2. Not accessible for analytics or modern workloads.
findings.recommendation: Migrate data to S3. Use S3 event notifications for downstream processing. Implement Athena/Glue for analytics.

findings.title: Data Access Layer — no abstraction
findings.description: Data access directly embedded in COBOL program. File I/O interleaved with business logic. No repository pattern or DAO layer.
findings.gap: No data access abstraction. File access, record parsing, and business logic all mixed in single program.
findings.recommendation: Implement clear data access layer (repository pattern) separating data retrieval from calculation logic.

findings.title: Database Engine EOL — DB2 v10 past end-of-support
findings.description: IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 past end-of-support since April 2020. No version pinning in IaC (no IaC exists). Unsupported for 5+ years.
findings.gap: Database engine past EOL 5+ years. No security patches, no vendor support, compliance risk.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported managed engine: Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Use AWS SCT and DMS.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — no encryption on PII data
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Employee PII (SSN, bank accounts) stored unencrypted on mainframe and EC2 gateway.
findings.gap: Zero encryption at rest. Sensitive PII stored unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt all data stores with customer-managed KMS keys. Enable encryption on RDS, S3, EBS.

findings.title: API Authentication — plaintext FTP credentials only
findings.description: No API authentication. FTP uses plaintext username/password hardcoded in JCL. No OAuth2, JWT, or token-based auth.
findings.gap: No modern authentication. FTP credentials hardcoded and transmitted in cleartext.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT via API Gateway + Cognito. Use AWS Transfer Family with IAM for file transfers.

findings.title: Centralized Identity — no IdP integration
findings.description: No centralized identity provider. Single hardcoded username/password for FTP. No Cognito, OIDC/SAML, or SSO.
findings.gap: No identity provider integration. Single shared credential with no user attribution.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Cognito or corporate directory). Implement per-user RBAC.

findings.title: Secrets Management — plaintext credentials in source control
findings.description: Plaintext credentials committed to source control: FTP password 'PayR0ll2003!' in JCL. No secrets manager or vault.
findings.gap: Critical: plaintext password in version-controlled source file. Deployment-blocking security issue.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate exposed credential. Store all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — no patching or scanning
findings.description: No patching strategy or vulnerability scanning. EC2 gateway has no SSM, no Inspector. Running unsupported DB2 v10.
findings.gap: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, no compute hardening.
findings.recommendation: Use hardened images (Bottlerocket, AL2023), enable SSM Patch Manager, integrate Inspector/Snyk, configure Dependabot.

findings.title: Security Pipeline — no scanning tools
findings.description: No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate security tools into.
findings.gap: Zero security scanning. No automated vulnerability detection.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (Semgrep), dependency scanning (Dependabot/Snyk), container scanning (ECR) with blocking gates.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — no instrumentation
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or trace ID propagation. COBOL program has no observability.
findings.gap: No tracing. Failures diagnosed only via mainframe SYSOUT logs.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry from the start when building new service.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — no formal SLOs
findings.description: No SLOs defined. Only implicit SLO is batch window constraint which is informal and not monitored. Batch 'sometimes overruns.'
findings.gap: No formal SLO definitions. SLO violations occurring without tracking or alerting.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: batch completion time, error rate (zero tolerance for payroll errors), availability targets.

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No tracking of employees processed, payroll amounts, processing time, or error rates.
findings.gap: No business metrics. Cannot measure outcomes, detect anomalies, or track efficiency.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics to CloudWatch: employees processed, total disbursed, errors, duration.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection — no alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection. Batch overruns detected manually the next business day.
findings.gap: No alerting. Failures detected only when downstream consumers notice missing output.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms on completion time, error rates, record count anomalies. Configure PagerDuty.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no automated tests exist
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README: 'No automated tests; changes validated in a shared QA region only.' Zero test coverage.
findings.gap: Zero automated testing. Changes to payroll calculations have no automated verification.
findings.recommendation: Document expected outputs for known inputs. Build comprehensive test suite covering all tax calculations and edge cases.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — no monitoring assets exist
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarms with owners, no SLO definitions.
findings.gap: No observability assets exist to own.
findings.recommendation: Establish observability ownership from day one: per-service dashboards, alarms with team owners, SLOs.
